description: Sample GATE EE question bank (30 original questions) showing the bank format

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.question: Choose the word that best completes the sentence: The committee's decision was ______; no amount of argument afterwards could change it.
questions.solution: The second clause says nothing could change the decision, so the decision was final and unalterable: 'irrevocable'.
questions.common_trap: Picking 'tentative' or 'provisional' by reading only the first clause.
questions.distractor_logic: A and D mean the opposite (open to change); C describes clarity, not finality.

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.question: Pipe A fills a tank in 12 hours and pipe B fills it in 15 hours. Pipe C empties the full tank in 20 hours. If all three pipes are opened together on an empty tank, the time taken to fill the tank is ______ hours (round off to the nearest integer).
questions.solution: Net rate = 1/12 + 1/15 - 1/20 = (5 + 4 - 3)/60 = 6/60 = 1/10 tank per hour, so the tank fills in 10 hours.
questions.concept: Combined work rates with an outlet
questions.common_trap: Adding the outlet rate instead of subtracting it (gives 5 h).

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.question: Five people P, Q, R, S and T sit in a row facing north. Q sits immediately to the right of P. S sits between T and P and is adjacent to both. R sits at one of the ends and T does not sit at an end. Who sits in the middle?
questions.solution: Q is immediately right of P and S is adjacent to both T and P, so S must be left of P: T S P Q. R is at an end. If R is at the right end, T is at the left end, which is not allowed. So the order is R T S P Q and the middle seat is S.
questions.common_trap: Ignoring the condition that T is not at an end, which also allows T S P Q R (middle P).
questions.distractor_logic: A is the answer if the last condition is skipped; B and D come from placing S to the right of P.

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question: Let A = [[2, 1], [1, 2]]. The eigenvalues of the matrix B = A^2 - 2A + I, where I is the 2x2 identity matrix, are
questions.solution: The eigenvalues of A are 1 and 3. B = (A - I)^2, so its eigenvalues are (1 - 1)^2 = 0 and (3 - 1)^2 = 4.
questions.common_trap: Reporting the eigenvalues of A^2 (1 and 9) and forgetting the other terms.
questions.distractor_logic: A: eigenvalues of A^2 only; C: eigenvalues of A - 2I (the A^2 term dropped); D: forgetting to square (A - I).

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question: The value of the integral of sin^2(x) cos^2(x) dx from x = 0 to x = pi/2 is ______ (round off to 3 decimal places).
questions.solution: sin^2 x cos^2 x = sin^2(2x)/4 = (1 - cos 4x)/8. Integrating from 0 to pi/2 gives (1/8)(pi/2) - 0 = pi/16 = 0.196.
questions.common_trap: Writing sin x cos x = sin 2x (dropping the 1/2), which gives 4 times the correct value (pi/4).

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question: A random variable X follows a Poisson distribution with mean 2. Which of the following statements is/are TRUE?
questions.solution: P(X = k) = e^-2 2^k / k!. (A) P(X = 0) = e^-2: true. (B) E[X^2] = Var(X) + (E[X])^2 = 2 + 4 = 6: true. (C) Var(X) = mean = 2, not 4: false. (D) P(X = 1) = 2e^-2 and P(X = 2) = 4e^-2/2 = 2e^-2: true.
questions.common_trap: Taking the variance as the square of the mean.
questions.distractor_logic: C tempts students who treat Poisson variance like the square of the mean.

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.subtopic: Higher-order linear ODEs with constant coefficients
questions.question: The solution of y'' + 4y' + 4y = 0 with y(0) = 1 and y'(0) = 0 is
questions.solution: The characteristic equation m^2 + 4m + 4 = 0 has a repeated root m = -2, so y = (c1 + c2 t)e^-2t. y(0) = c1 = 1. y'(0) = c2 - 2c1 = 0 gives c2 = 2. So y = (1 + 2t)e^-2t.
questions.common_trap: Taking y'(0) = c2 and missing the -2c1 term, which gives c2 = 0 and y = e^(-2t).
questions.distractor_logic: B: sign error in the derivative; C: halves c2; D: drops the -2c1 term so c2 = 0.

questions.subject: Electric Circuits
questions.question: A 12 V ideal DC source in series with a 4 ohm resistor feeds node a. A 6 ohm resistor connects node a to the reference node. A 1.6 ohm resistor connects node a to terminal x, and a variable load resistor RL is connected between terminal x and the reference node. The maximum power that can be delivered to RL is ______ W (round off to 2 decimal places).
questions.solution: Thevenin voltage at x: Vth = 12 x 6/(4 + 6) = 7.2 V (no current in the 1.6 ohm resistor on open circuit). Rth = (4 || 6) + 1.6 = 2.4 + 1.6 = 4 ohm. Pmax = Vth^2/(4 Rth) = 51.84/16 = 3.24 W.
questions.concept: Thevenin equivalent with a series element, then maximum power transfer
questions.common_trap: Forgetting the 1.6 ohm series resistor in Rth (gives 5.40 W).

questions.subject: Electric Circuits
questions.question: A 10 microfarad capacitor, initially charged to 2 V, is connected at t = 0 to a 10 V DC source through a 10 kilo-ohm resistor. The capacitor voltage at t = 0.1 s is approximately
questions.concept: First-order response with a non-zero initial condition
questions.common_trap: Ignoring the initial 2 V and using 10(1 - e^-1) = 6.32 V.
questions.distractor_logic: A: zero initial condition; C: initial plus 6 V without the exponential; D: the exponential term alone.

questions.subject: Electric Circuits
questions.question: In the two-wattmeter method of measuring power in a balanced three-phase load, the wattmeters read 2000 W and 1000 W. The power factor of the load is
questions.solution: tan(phi) = sqrt(3)(W1 - W2)/(W1 + W2) = sqrt(3) x 1000/3000 = 0.577, so phi = 30 degrees and pf = cos 30 = 0.866.
questions.common_trap: Dropping the sqrt(3) factor, giving tan(phi) = 1/3 and pf = 0.949.
questions.distractor_logic: B: pf when one reading is zero; C: random 45 degrees; D: missed sqrt(3).

questions.subject: Electromagnetic Fields
questions.question: An air-filled parallel-plate capacitor has capacitance C0. A dielectric slab of relative permittivity 4, with the same area as the plates and thickness equal to half the plate separation, is inserted parallel to the plates. The new capacitance is
questions.solution: The slab and the remaining air gap act as capacitors in series: 2C0 (air, d/2) and 8C0 (dielectric, d/2). C = (2C0 x 8C0)/(10C0) = 1.6 C0.
questions.common_trap: Treating the layers as parallel and averaging permittivities: (1 + 4)/2 = 2.5 C0.
questions.distractor_logic: A: parallel combination; C: whole gap filled; D: only the air half doubled.

questions.subject: Electromagnetic Fields
questions.question: A toroidal core has a mean iron path length of 0.5 m, a cross-sectional area of 4 cm^2 and relative permeability 1000. It has an air gap of 1 mm and carries a 500-turn coil. Neglecting fringing and leakage, the coil current needed to produce a flux of 0.4 mWb in the gap is ______ A (round off to 2 decimal places).
questions.concept: Series magnetic circuit with an air gap
questions.common_trap: Ignoring the air gap reluctance (gives 0.80 A) even though the gap dominates.

questions.subject: Signals and Systems
questions.question: The signal x(t) = cos(200 pi t) + cos(500 pi t) is sampled at 400 samples/s and passed through an ideal low-pass filter with cut-off 200 Hz. The output contains frequency components at
questions.solution: The components are 100 Hz and 250 Hz. With fs = 400 Hz, 250 Hz is above fs/2 = 200 Hz and aliases to 400 - 250 = 150 Hz. The filter passes 100 Hz and 150 Hz.
questions.common_trap: Assuming both components are reproduced because fs exceeds the highest frequency (but not twice it).
questions.distractor_logic: A: no aliasing considered; C: aliased component assumed removed; D: radian-to-Hz confusion (dividing by 4 pi).

questions.subject: Signals and Systems
questions.question: An LTI system has impulse response h(t) = e^(-t) u(t). The input is x(t) = u(t) - u(t - 2). The output y(t) at t = 3 s is ______ (round off to 3 decimal places).
questions.solution: y(3) = integral of x(tau) h(3 - tau) dtau from 0 to 2 = integral of e^-(3 - tau) dtau from 0 to 2 = e^-3 (e^2 - 1) = e^-1 - e^-3 = 0.368 - 0.050 = 0.318.
questions.common_trap: Integrating up to t = 3 instead of the pulse end at 2 (gives 0.950).

questions.subject: Electrical Machines
questions.question: A 20 kVA, 2000/200 V single-phase transformer has a core loss of 200 W and a full-load copper loss of 400 W. Its efficiency at the load at which efficiency is maximum, at 0.8 power factor lagging, is ______ % (round off to 2 decimal places).
questions.solution: Maximum efficiency occurs when copper loss = core loss, at load fraction x = sqrt(200/400) = 0.7071. Output = 0.7071 x 20000 x 0.8 = 11313.7 W. Losses = 200 + 200 = 400 W. Efficiency = 11313.7/11713.7 = 96.59%.
questions.common_trap: Computing efficiency at full load (96.39%) instead of at the maximum-efficiency load.

questions.subject: Electrical Machines
questions.question: A 4-pole, 50 Hz, three-phase slip-ring induction motor has rotor resistance 0.2 ohm per phase and standstill rotor reactance 1.0 ohm per phase (both referred to the stator). Neglect stator impedance. Which of the following statements is/are TRUE?
options: Speed at maximum torque is 1200 rpm
An external resistance of 1.0 ohm per phase in the rotor gives maximum torque at starting
The value of maximum torque does not depend on rotor resistance
questions.solution: Slip at maximum torque sm = R2/X2 = 0.2 (A true). Speed = 1500(1 - 0.2) = 1200 rpm (B true). For maximum torque at start, R2 + Rext = X2, so Rext = 0.8 ohm, not 1.0 ohm (C false). Tmax is proportional to V^2/(2X2) and independent of R2 (D true).
questions.concept: Maximum torque condition and effect of rotor resistance
questions.common_trap: Setting Rext = X2 instead of R2 + Rext = X2.
questions.distractor_logic: C is the classic Rext = X2 error.

questions.subject: Electrical Machines
questions.question: A 220 V DC shunt motor has armature resistance 0.5 ohm and draws an armature current of 40 A at 1000 rpm. With field current and load torque unchanged, the external resistance to be inserted in series with the armature to reduce the speed to 800 rpm is ______ ohm (round off to 2 decimal places).
questions.solution: Constant torque and flux mean Ia stays at 40 A. Eb1 = 220 - 40 x 0.5 = 200 V. Eb2 = 200 x 800/1000 = 160 V. 220 - 40(0.5 + R) = 160 gives R = 1.0 ohm.
questions.concept: Armature resistance speed control at constant torque
questions.common_trap: Scaling the supply voltage by the speed ratio instead of the back emf.

questions.subject: Electrical Machines
questions.question: A synchronous motor drives a constant load at unity power factor. If its field current is increased beyond this value, the armature current
options: decreases and the power factor becomes lagging
increases and the power factor becomes leading
increases and the power factor becomes lagging
decreases and the power factor becomes leading
questions.solution: Beyond normal excitation the motor is over-excited: it supplies reactive power to the system, the power factor becomes leading and the armature current rises along the right arm of the V-curve.
questions.common_trap: Mixing up generator and motor conventions and choosing lagging.
questions.distractor_logic: C applies to under-excitation; A and D wrongly assume unity pf is not the minimum-current point.

questions.subject: Power Systems
questions.question: A generator reactance is 0.2 pu on a 50 MVA, 11 kV base. On a 100 MVA, 22 kV base, its reactance is
questions.solution: Z_new = Z_old (S_new/S_old)(V_old/V_new)^2 = 0.2 x 2 x (11/22)^2 = 0.2 x 2 x 0.25 = 0.1 pu.
questions.common_trap: Inverting the voltage ratio, giving 0.2 x 2 x 4 = 1.6 pu, or the MVA ratio, giving 0.025 pu.
questions.distractor_logic: B: MVA ratio only; C: voltage ratio not squared and inverted; D: MVA ratio inverted.

questions.subject: Power Systems
questions.question: An unloaded generator with solidly grounded neutral has E = 1.0 pu, X1 = 0.2 pu, X2 = 0.15 pu and X0 = 0.05 pu. The fault current for a bolted single line-to-ground fault at its terminals is
questions.solution: For an LG fault the three sequence networks are in series: Ia1 = E/(X1 + X2 + X0) = 1/0.4 = 2.5 pu. Fault current = 3 Ia1 = 7.5 pu.
questions.concept: Sequence network connection for an LG fault
questions.common_trap: Reporting the sequence current Ia1 (2.5 pu) as the fault current.
questions.distractor_logic: B: forgets the factor 3; C: three-phase fault current E/X1; D: drops X0 from the series sum.

questions.subject: Power Systems
questions.question: A generator delivers 1.0 pu to an infinite bus with Pmax = 2.0 pu, so the initial load angle is 30 degrees. A three-phase fault at the generator terminals reduces the electrical output to zero and is then cleared, restoring the original network. Using the equal area criterion, the critical clearing angle is ______ degrees (round off to 2 decimal places).
questions.solution: delta0 = 30 deg = 0.5236 rad, delta_max = 180 - 30 = 150 deg = 2.618 rad. cos(delta_c) = (Pm/Pmax)(delta_max - delta0) + cos(delta_max) = 0.5 x 2.0944 - 0.8660 = 0.1812, so delta_c = 79.56 degrees.
questions.concept: Equal area criterion with zero power during the fault
questions.common_trap: Using degrees instead of radians for (delta_max - delta0) inside the formula.

questions.subject: Control Systems
questions.question: The characteristic equation of a closed-loop system is s^3 + 2s^2 + Ks + 8 = 0. The system is stable for
questions.solution: Routh array: s^3: 1, K; s^2: 2, 8; s^1: (2K - 8)/2; s^0: 8. Stability needs 2K - 8 > 0, i.e. K > 4.
questions.common_trap: Using the product condition a1 a2 > a0 a3 incorrectly as K > 8.

questions.subject: Control Systems
questions.question: A unity-feedback system has open-loop transfer function G(s) = K/(s(s + 4)). K is chosen so that the closed-loop damping ratio is 0.5. The resulting peak overshoot of the unit-step response is ______ % (round off to 2 decimal places).
questions.solution: Closed loop: s^2 + 4s + K. 2 zeta wn = 4 with zeta = 0.5 gives wn = 4 and K = 16. Mp = exp(-pi zeta/sqrt(1 - zeta^2)) = exp(-1.8138) = 0.1630, i.e. 16.30%.
questions.common_trap: Using exp(-pi zeta) without the sqrt(1 - zeta^2) term (gives 20.79%).

questions.subject: Control Systems
questions.question: A unity-feedback system has open-loop transfer function G(s) = 10/(s(s + 1)(s + 10)). Which of the following statements is/are TRUE?
options: The velocity error constant Kv is 1
The steady-state error for a unit-step input is zero
The initial slope of the Bode magnitude plot is -20 dB/decade
The phase angle tends to -180 degrees as frequency tends to infinity
questions.solution: Kv = lim s G(s) as s -> 0 = 10/10 = 1 (A true). It is a type-1 system, so the steady-state error to a unit step is zero (B true). The integrator gives an initial Bode slope of -20 dB/decade (C true). With three poles, the phase tends to -270 degrees, not -180 degrees (D false).
questions.concept: System type, error constants and Bode asymptotes
questions.common_trap: Counting only the finite poles when finding the high-frequency phase.

questions.subject: Electrical and Electronic Measurements
questions.question: A PMMC instrument with internal resistance 5 ohm gives full-scale deflection at 10 mA. The shunt resistance needed to use it as a 0-1 A ammeter is approximately
questions.solution: Shunt current = 1 - 0.01 = 0.99 A. Rsh = Im Rm/(I - Im) = 0.01 x 5/0.99 = 0.0505 ohm.
questions.common_trap: Using Rm/(I/Im) = 0.05 ohm, which forgets that the meter itself carries 10 mA.
questions.distractor_logic: B: multiplying factor not reduced by one; C: series multiplier formula; D: decimal slip.

questions.subject: Electrical and Electronic Measurements
questions.question: Power is computed as P = I^2 R, with I = 2 A +/- 1% and R = 100 ohm +/- 0.5%. The limiting error in P is +/- ______ %.
questions.solution: For a product of powers, relative limiting errors add with the exponents as weights: 2(1%) + 0.5% = 2.5%.
questions.common_trap: Adding 1% + 0.5% = 1.5% and ignoring the square on I.

questions.subject: Analog and Digital Electronics
questions.question: An inverting Schmitt trigger uses an op-amp with output saturation of +/-12 V. The output feeds back to the non-inverting input through R2 = 50 kilo-ohm, and R1 = 10 kilo-ohm connects the non-inverting input to ground. Which of the following statements is/are TRUE?
options: The upper threshold voltage is +2 V
The output switches to -12 V when the input rises above the upper threshold
The threshold voltages depend on the input signal frequency
questions.solution: Feedback fraction = R1/(R1 + R2) = 10/60. UTP = +12/6 = +2 V and LTP = -2 V (A true), so the hysteresis width is 4 V (B true). In the inverting configuration, the output switches to -12 V when the input rises above UTP (C true). The thresholds depend only on the resistors and the saturation levels, not on input frequency (D false).
questions.common_trap: Using R2/(R1 + R2) as the feedback fraction, giving thresholds of +/-10 V.

questions.subject: Analog and Digital Electronics
questions.question: The minimal sum-of-products form of F(A, B, C) = sum of minterms m(0, 2, 4, 5, 6) is
questions.solution: Minterms 0, 2, 4 and 6 all have C = 0, giving C'. Minterm 5 (101) pairs with 4 (100) to give AB'. F = C' + AB'.
questions.common_trap: Grouping 5 with 7 (not a minterm) to get AC.

questions.subject: Power Electronics
questions.question: An ideal buck converter operates from 48 V at a switching frequency of 50 kHz with duty ratio 0.5. It has L = 100 microhenry and supplies a 6 ohm resistive load. The peak inductor current is ______ A (round off to 1 decimal place).
questions.solution: Vo = D Vin = 24 V, Io = 24/6 = 4 A. Ripple = (Vin - Vo) D/(L f) = 24 x 0.5/(100e-6 x 50e3) = 2.4 A. The minimum current 4 - 1.2 = 2.8 A > 0, so the converter is in CCM. Peak = 4 + 1.2 = 5.2 A.
questions.concept: Inductor ripple and CCM check in a buck converter
questions.common_trap: Adding the full ripple instead of half (gives 6.4 A).

questions.subject: Power Electronics
questions.question: A single-phase fully controlled bridge converter is fed from 230 V (rms), 50 Hz and supplies a highly inductive load so the current is continuous. At a firing angle of 60 degrees, the average output voltage is approximately
questions.solution: Vo = (2 Vm/pi) cos(alpha) = (2 x 325.27/pi) x 0.5 = 103.5 V.
questions.concept: Average output of a full converter in continuous conduction
questions.common_trap: Using the semi-converter expression (Vm/pi)(1 + cos alpha), which gives 155.3 V.
questions.distractor_logic: B: semi-converter formula; C: alpha = 0; D: half-wave converter.
